docs.title: mibpkg
docs.text:
An app store and package manager for the MIB2 High head unit.

mibpkg installs, updates, removes and rolls back software on the car. It serves a phone-friendly web interface from the unit itself, and also has an in-car menu. A supervisor starts your services at boot and restarts them if they die.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Install

    Put the SD card together and install mibpkg from the engineering menu.

  • First use

    Join the hotspot and open the web interface.

  • Packages

    Install, update, remove and roll back software.

  • Your first package

    Build a .mpk, test it, and publish a collection cars can update from.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Web interface on the car — Discover, Updates, Installed and More, from a phone.
  • .mpk packages — a gzip'd tar with a manifest.toml, files, services, configs and scripts.
  • One package per product — a native daemon and its SDK status plugin can ship together.
  • Online sources — add a collection by github:owner/repo; the car checks for updates.
  • Recovery — atomic installs, backups, rollback, a DISABLE card and web-settings recovery.

docs.title: Supported units
docs.text:
Unit MIB2 High, model MHI2 or MHI2Q OS QNX 6.5 Package format .mpk Web interface Hotspot and Tailscale by default

See Units for compatibility and [compat].

docs.title: Status
docs.text: mibpkg 0.10.0. The docs describe the current main branch.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: mibpkg is a Rust binary, an on-unit web app and a small set of shell/Python/Gradle tools around it.

docs.title: Good places to start
docs.text:
• A package recipe or example that shows a pattern the docs do not.
  • A web interface fix or a JSON API improvement.
  • A test that reproduces a package or supervisor bug.
  • A documentation fix.

docs.title: Ground rules
docs.text:
• The unit has a small, old QNX userland. Do not assume printf, which, cmp, od, uniq or mkfifo.
  • /tmp is /dev/shmem: files only, no directories.
  • /mnt/app is normally read-only; follow the remount holder protocol.
  • A package runs as root. Do not add a feature that hides what a package does.
  • Keep the package format and the web API backward compatible unless you bump the version and document the change.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Open an issue or comment on one.
  2. Branch from main.
  3. Add tests.
  4. Run the gates in Test.
  5. Update the docs and CHANGELOG.md in the same change.
  6. Open a pull request.

The unit binary is cross-compiled for QNX 6.5 ARMv7 in a Docker image:

It needs Docker Desktop with Rosetta enabled on Apple silicon and the qnx65-armv7-toolchain:8.5-rust image.

Output:

out/sd/
out/mibpkg-sd-<version>.zip

scripts/bundle.sh builds the host binary, stages the unit binary, builds the official collection and calls mibpkg swdl-card. Pass --signed-header FILE to make the engineering-menu entry accepted.

docs.title: Web assets
docs.text:
web/ is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step. The files are embedded in the binary as written.

For local development:

MIBPKG_WEB_DIR=web ./target/debug/mibpkg --root /tmp/mibpkg-fixture web

  • Active voice, present tense.
  • Short sentences and paragraphs.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
• Every page answers one question.
  • Prerequisites near the top.
  • A runnable command or example before the long explanation.
  • End with a Related list, not a summary.
  • Exact fields, limits and commands belong in Reference; guides explain the shape.
Type Use it for Tutorial A first complete success Guide A task an experienced reader dips into Reference Exact names, fields, defaults and errors Explanation Architecture, trade-offs and why

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Every command must run as written from the stated directory.
  • Use sh for shell blocks and toml for manifests.
  • Never invent a command or a field. Check src/cli.rs and src/manifest.rs.
  • Keep example manifests short; link to real packages for the full version.

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text:
• Use Material admonitions: note, tip, warning, danger.
  • Use tables for reference data.
  • Use Mermaid for flows and architecture.
  • Use repo-relative links for files and full URLs for the published site.

docs.title: What not to write
docs.text:
• OEM vehicle-brand names in public docs.
  • Internal paths, plan names or task numbers.
  • Machine-specific paths, IP addresses or personal data.
  • The future as if it were shipped.

docs.title: Brand names
docs.text: Public docs keep platform codes (MIB2, MHI2, MHI2Q) and third-party tool names (M.I.B., GEM). They do not name vehicle manufacturers. tools/check_docs.py enforces the rule.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
mibpkg is one Rust binary with two lives: host tooling and an on-unit package manager.

flowchart TB
    subgraph host["Host"]
        BUILD["mibpkg build / index"]
        RELEASE["mibpkg release / verify"]
        ACTION["GitHub Action"]
    end
    subgraph unit["Unit"]
        CLI["mibpkg CLI"]
        SUP["supervisor"]
        WEB["web server"]
        GEM["GEM screens"]
        PKGS["installed packages"]
    end
    BUILD --> RELEASE
    RELEASE -->|GitHub release| WEB
    ACTION --> RELEASE
    CLI --> PKGS
    SUP --> PKGS
    WEB --> CLI
    GEM --> CLI

docs.title: Host tooling
docs.text:
Host commands build and publish:

  • mibpkg build — a .mpk from a source directory.
  • mibpkg index — index.json for a collection.
  • mibpkg release — a GitHub release with the index and packages.
  • mibpkg verify — check a collection or card the way a car would.
  • mibpkg new — a runnable package skeleton.

They use the same manifest parser and archive code as the unit, so a package that builds is a package the unit can read.

docs.title: On the unit
docs.text:
Component Role CLI Actions, installs, grants, SDK verbs Supervisor Starts and restarts services; runs the boot checks Web server The phone interface and JSON API GEM screens In-car status and recovery buttons Boot hook Starts the supervisor from startup.sh Package store /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/pkgs

The CLI and web server never run plugin code. A plugin runs in the SDK runtime; mibpkg only writes its jar and grants.

docs.title: Two packages, one product
docs.text:
A native daemon and its SDK status plugin ship as one package:

flowchart LR
    P["tailscale-1.102.5.mpk"] --> M["mibpkg install"]
    M --> A["pkgs/tailscale/1.102.5/<br/>bin/tailscaled"]
    M --> B["SDK plugins/<br/>tailscale-status.jar"]
    A --> S["supervisor: tailscale"]
    B --> R["SDK runtime: status item"]
    R -->|loopback query| S

The package name is the install/update identity. The plugin keeps its own id for grants, data, icons and reload. Removing the package removes both halves.

docs.title: The web server
docs.text:
The web server is a static bundle embedded in the binary. It serves:

  • the HTML/CSS/JS interface;
  • the JSON API;
  • uploads and job output.

It runs as the supervisor's mibpkg.web service. A self-update restarts it.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Area Purpose /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/pkgs Package files and versions /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/state Config, backups, boot entries, GEM data /mnt/persist/mibsdk SDK plugin data /tmp Runtime markers, logs, uploads

/mnt/app is normally read-only and is remounted for writes under a holder protocol. /tmp is RAM.

docs.title: Boot
docs.text:
The card installer adds a hook to startup.sh. On boot it:

  1. checks for mibpkg/DISABLE;
  2. starts the supervisor in the background;
  3. the supervisor starts the web server and the installed services.

The stock boot path still runs; mibpkg is an add-on, not a replacement.

docs.title: Supervisor
docs.text:
The supervisor:

  • reads the installed packages and their [[service]] entries;
  • waits for each service's after conditions;
  • starts services in the package order;
  • restarts them according to restart;
  • requests a reload when a package is installed, updated or removed;
  • runs the web server as mibpkg.web;
  • rewrites GEM screens and the status values.

It is a long-running process. mibpkg supervise runs it in the foreground.

docs.title: Start conditions
docs.text:
Common conditions:

Condition Waits for internet A default route tailnet A route to 100.100.100.100 through tun* hmi-ready The HMI startup marker file:/path A file iface:name An interface with an address route:dest A route

after_timeout starts the service anyway after the given time. See Service conditions.

docs.title: Restarts
docs.text:
Policy Behaviour always Restart whenever it exits on-failure Restart on a non-zero exit never Do not restart

A restart is requested through a marker in /tmp; the supervisor picks it up within a few seconds.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Service stdout/stderr goes to /tmp/mibpkg.<package>.<service>.log. The web page tails it. /tmp is RAM, so logs are capped and do not survive a reboot.

docs.title: If a service will not start
docs.text:
1. Check the package's config: a required file may be missing.
  2. Check its after conditions: the network or tailnet may not be up yet.
  3. Read its log.
  4. Restart it from the package page or mibpkg restart <name>.

docs.title: Install methods
docs.text: One card image installs through two paths.

docs.title: Engineering menu (SWDL)
docs.text:
The update menu reads metainfo2.txt at the card root. It runs the installer payload, which:

  1. copies mibpkg to /mnt/app/root/mibpkg;
  2. runs mibpkg bootstrap;
  3. adds the boot hook;
  4. enables the GEM entry;
  5. applies the GEM patch.

The menu requires a genuine, manufacturer-signed metainfo2 header. mibpkg cannot ship one; the release image includes the rest. A card without the header still works through the custom-script method.

docs.title: Custom script
docs.text: The card also carries a mod/ script. M.I.B.'s Run Custom Script runs it. The script installs the same payload and calls the same mibpkg bootstrap; it does not need the signed header.

docs.title: One card
docs.text:
The release image carries both paths:

/
├── metainfo2.txt
├── _Swdlautorun.txt
├── mibpkg/
└── mod/

mibpkg swdl-card assembles it. --no-mib emits a pure SWDL card.

docs.title: Which path is used
docs.text:
The unit picks the path you start:

  • Engineering menu → Update uses SWDL;
  • M.I.B. → Run Custom Script uses the script.

They do not run together.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Both paths install the same files, so either recovery path works:

  • GEM → mibpkg → Remove mibpkg;
  • mibpkg uninstall-self;
  • reinstall from the card.

Uninstall restores the stock files mibpkg backed up.

docs.title: Online updates
docs.text: mibpkg can check GitHub releases for new package versions.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
A source is a GitHub repository with releases made by mibpkg release:

  • index.json
  • package .mpk files
  • optional assets such as sources.json

Cars add github:owner/repo in More → Sources, or read it from the card's mibpkg/sources.toml.

The official collection is built in.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
The supervisor checks sources when the car has internet and periodically after boot. The web interface also refreshes on Updates.

For each package mibpkg keeps the newest compatible version across the loaded collections. An update is offered when the collection has a higher semver version than the installed one.

docs.title: Download and verify
docs.text:
For a remote package, mibpkg:

  1. resolves the index URL (GitHub's releases/latest/download redirect);
  2. downloads the index;
  3. downloads the package;
  4. checks its SHA-256 and size;
  5. checks the manifest, compatibility and, for plugins, the SDK and permissions;
  6. installs it.

A failed check changes nothing.

docs.title: Time and TLS
docs.text: The unit's clock is unset at boot, so mibpkg uses SNTP to establish a verification time. TLS uses the unit's libcurl and the CA bundle installed with mibpkg. A car that has never had a working network may need an online check after the clock is set.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text: The last index and packages are cached so Discover and Updates work offline. A source that cannot be reached is reported in More → Sources and Health; the card collections still work.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
mibpkg release:

  • builds each package;
  • carries older versions forward (--keep, default 3);
  • writes absolute download URLs;
  • creates the GitHub release;
  • waits for the new index to become live.

A version already published with different contents is refused. Bump the version.

docs.title: Safety and recovery
docs.text: mibpkg changes the head unit's software. The design assumes something will go wrong.

docs.title: Atomic installs
docs.text:
An install writes a new version directory and switches current only after everything is staged, config is imported, scripts have run and the plugin half (if any) is deployed. Before the switch, a failure removes the new directory and leaves the old version active.

Updates keep the previous version for rollback.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
The installer and some actions edit stock files:

  • startup.sh (the boot hook);
  • the bundle list;
  • GEM screens;
  • firewall config.

mibpkg stores a once-only backup of each file it touches under state/backups/. Uninstall restores them. A backup is written before the first change and never overwritten by a later install.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: mibpkg rollback <name> switches current to the previous version and restores its files, services and plugin half. A plugin's grants never grow on rollback: a permission that only the old version declares needs approval.

docs.title: Remount protocol
docs.text:
/mnt/app is normally read-only. Several processes remount it, so mibpkg uses a holder protocol:

  1. Take /tmp/mibpkg.rwlock (create-new, pid inside).
  2. Create /tmp/mibpkg.rw.app.<pid>.
  3. mount -uw /mnt/app.
  4. On release, remove the holder and run mount -ur only when no live holder remains.

Other tools that write /mnt/app should follow the same protocol. A 0.7 supervisor did not; that is why mibpkg re-asserts the mount before each write and verifies critical writes by reading them back.

docs.title: DISABLE
docs.text: mibpkg/DISABLE on the card stops everything at boot: no supervisor, no services, no web server. It is the safest way to get a misbehaving unit back to stock behaviour without uninstalling.

docs.title: Vehicle overrides
docs.text: The SDK can hold a vehicle override (for example parking tones). Its ledger restores the prior value when the plugin is removed, disabled or the ignition goes off. mibpkg refuses to remove the SDK while an override is pending unless --force is used.

docs.title: What mibpkg does not do
docs.text:
• It does not sandbox a package. A package runs as root, like the rest of the unit's software.
  • It does not protect against a malicious package. Install only sources you trust.
  • It does not make a bad firmware update safe. Backups are for mibpkg's own changes.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
This section takes you from an SD card to mibpkg running on the unit.

  • Requirements

    The unit, the card, the computer and the image.

  • Install

    The engineering-menu method: format, copy, install, reboot.

  • Custom-script install

    The alternative if you already use M.I.B.

  • First use

    Join the hotspot, open the web interface, install your first package.

  • Update mibpkg

    Self-update from the web interface or from a card.

  • Remove and recover

    Uninstall, reset a PIN, or stop everything with DISABLE.

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
1. Download mibpkg-sd-<version>.zip.
  2. Unzip it to the root of a FAT32 SD card partitioned with Master Boot Record.
  3. Insert the card in SD1, open engineering menu → Update → Standard, select mibpkg and start.
  4. When the unit settles, join its Wi-Fi hotspot and open GEM → mibpkg for the web address.

docs.title: Open the web interface
docs.text:
1. Join the car's Wi-Fi hotspot from your phone, or reach the car over Tailscale.
  2. In the car, open GEM → mibpkg. It shows the address, for example http://10.255.1.1.
  3. Open that address in your phone's browser.

The interface has four tabs:

Tab What it does Discover Browse packages on the card and online collections Updates See available updates and update everything Installed Inspect, configure, restart, roll back or remove packages More Install from file, logs, sources, web settings, health

docs.title: Install a package
docs.text:
1. Open Discover.
  2. Tap a package.
  3. Tap Install.
  4. Approve any permissions the package asks for.

A plugin package's permissions are shown in plain words. A package that adds a permission needs explicit approval.

docs.title: Install a .mpk from your phone
docs.text:
1. Open More → Install from file.
  2. Choose the .mpk file.
  3. Review the package, its compatibility and any permissions.
  4. Install.

Uploads expire after 10 minutes if you do not install them.

docs.title: Update everything
docs.text: Open Updates → Update all. A plugin update that adds a permission is not approved for you; install that plugin individually with Install or Update so you can review the new permission.

docs.title: Set a PIN
docs.text: Open More → Web settings. A PIN is 4 to 12 digits. If you forget it, use GEM → mibpkg → Remove PIN. If the web settings lock you out, use GEM → mibpkg → Reset web settings.

docs.title: Emergency stop
docs.text: Create an empty file mibpkg/DISABLE on the SD card and reboot. No package services start while it is present. Remove it and reboot to resume.

docs.title: Custom-script install
docs.text: If the unit already runs M.I.B., you can install mibpkg with its script runner instead of the engineering-menu update. The card image is the same; one card works for both methods.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Unzip mibpkg-sd-<version>.zip onto the M.I.B. SD card.
  2. Insert the card.
  3. Open GEM → M.I.B. → Advanced Settings → Run Custom Script.
  4. Wait for the script to finish.
  5. Open GEM → mibpkg, or the web interface.

The script installs the payload, starts the supervisor and adds the GEM entry. It does not need the signed engineering-menu header.

docs.title: Which method should I use?
docs.text:
Engineering menu Custom script Needs M.I.B. No Yes Needs a signed header Yes, for the update menu to accept the entry No Installs the same payload Yes Yes Recovery GEM → mibpkg GEM → mibpkg

The engineering-menu method is the normal path for a new unit. Use the custom-script method if M.I.B. is already set up and you prefer one tap.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: This is the engineering-menu method. It needs no other software on the unit and is the recommended path.

docs.title: 1. Format the SD card
docs.text:
The unit reads cards partitioned with the Master Boot Record (MBR) scheme. A card formatted with GUID/GPT makes the SD-card option in the update menu greyed out.

macOSWindows
  1. Open Disk Utility and choose View → Show All Devices.
  2. Select the whole SD card device, not the volume under it.
  3. Click Erase, set Format to MS-DOS (FAT) and Scheme to Master Boot Record.
  4. Erase.

Use SD Memory Card Formatter, or diskpart. The card must end up FAT32 on an MBR disk, not a single GUID/GPT partition.

docs.title: 2. Copy the image
docs.text:
Unzip mibpkg-sd-<version>.zip and copy its contents to the root of the card, so metainfo2.txt sits at the top level next to mibpkg/ and mod/.

/
├── metainfo2.txt
├── _Swdlautorun.txt
├── mibpkg/
└── mod/

Eject the card safely.

docs.title: 3. Insert the card in SD1
docs.text: Put it in the unit's SD card 1 slot.

docs.title: 4. Open the engineering menu
docs.text: Open the engineering (Red) menu and choose Software Update. Select SD card 1.

docs.title: 5. Start the update
docs.text:
Choose Standard. Scroll to the bottom of the list: mibpkg is marked [Y]. The stock rows show [N/A]; that is normal. Select Start update.

Building your own card

The engineering menu accepts only a card with a genuine signed metainfo2 header. The release image includes one. If you build a card with scripts/bundle.sh, pass --signed-header <file>; without it, use the custom-script method.

docs.title: 6. Wait for the reboots
docs.text: The install runs and the unit restarts a few times. Do not pull the card or cut power.

docs.title: 7. Open mibpkg
docs.text:
The main interface is the web page served by the car. Join the unit's Wi-Fi hotspot and open GEM → mibpkg for the address. See First use.

The in-car GEM → mibpkg screen is the backup interface: it shows the address and has recovery buttons for a forgotten PIN, broken web settings, and removing mibpkg.

docs.title: If the SD-card option is greyed out
docs.text: The card is not MBR/FAT32. Reformat it and try again.

docs.title: Remove a package
docs.text:
Open Installed, select the package and choose Remove. A plugin's data is kept by default so a reinstall starts where it left off. Choose Remove and delete data to purge it.

From the command line:

mibpkg remove <name>
mibpkg remove <name> --purge

docs.title: Remove mibpkg
docs.text:
Use GEM → mibpkg → Remove mibpkg, or:

mibpkg uninstall-self
mibpkg uninstall-self --purge

Uninstalling restores the stock files mibpkg backed up. It refuses while packages, plugins or vehicle overrides are still active; remove those first, or use --force only if you understand the risk.

docs.title: Stop everything without uninstalling
docs.text:
Create an empty file mibpkg/DISABLE on the SD card and reboot:

mkdir -p /path/to/card/mibpkg
: > /path/to/card/mibpkg/DISABLE

The boot hook logs it and starts nothing. Remove the file and reboot to resume.

docs.title: Forgotten PIN
docs.text: GEM → mibpkg → Remove PIN. This clears the PIN and restarts the web server.

docs.title: Locked out of the web interface
docs.text: GEM → mibpkg → Reset web settings. This deletes web.toml, restores the defaults and restarts the web server.

docs.title: A package keeps failing
docs.text:
1. Open Installed → the package → Logs.
  2. Check More → Health.
  3. Roll back to the previous version from the package page.
  4. If the package will not start, remove it; its data is kept by default.

docs.title: The unit
docs.text:
mibpkg runs on a MIB2 High unit, model MHI2 or MHI2Q, on QNX 6.5. You do not need to tell the two models apart to install.

To check:

  1. In the car, hold NAV/MAP and MEDIA together for about 7 seconds to open the engineering menu.
  2. Choose Version information.
  3. The Current version line starts with MHI2 or MHI2Q on a supported unit.
  4. Hold NAV/MAP and MEDIA again to leave the menu; Back does not exit it.

Warning

Other MIB2 variants and other platforms are not supported. The package format and the boot hook are specific to the MIB2 High.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: Item Notes An SD card Any size; 2 GB is plenty A computer with an SD reader macOS, Windows or Linux mibpkg-sd-<version>.zip The release image About 15 minutes The unit reboots a few times during install

docs.title: What the installer changes
docs.text:
mibpkg installs on the writable app partition. It does not reflash the IFS image. It adds:

  • the mibpkg directory and its collection;
  • a boot hook that starts the supervisor;
  • a GEM entry for the status and recovery buttons;
  • firewall rules for the web interface on the hotspot.

Every stock file it touches is backed up once, and uninstalling restores it. See Safety and recovery.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Install

docs.title: From the web interface
docs.text:
Open Updates. When a newer mibpkg is available, its row shows Update to <version>. Tap it. The server restarts on the new version; the page reloads and asks for the PIN again if one is set.

The update comes from the official collection, or from a card if the card carries a newer version.

docs.title: From a card
docs.text:
1. Copy the new mibpkg-sd-<version>.zip contents to the card.
  2. Open More → Rescan (or Updates).
  3. Install the newer mibpkg from Updates.

docs.title: Check for online updates
docs.text: The supervisor checks online sources periodically when the car has internet. You can also open Updates and refresh. More → Sources shows the enabled collections.

docs.title: If the update fails
docs.text:
• The old version keeps running until the new one is committed.
  • mibpkg status and More → Health show the installed version and the supervisor's version.
  • If the web server does not come back, use GEM → mibpkg → Reset web settings or reboot.

See Safety and recovery.

docs.title: Config files
docs.text:
A package declares config files in its manifest:

[[config]]
path = "carmqtt.toml"
example = "carmqtt.toml.example"
required = true

The example is shipped in the package. The live file lives in the package's config directory:

/mnt/app/root/mibpkg/state/config/<package>/<path>

On the card, you can supply a config at:

mibpkg/config/<package>/<path>

Rescan imports new card configs. A config can be:

  • required — the service will not start until it exists;
  • optional — the example is copied only when the user asks, or when the package needs it.

docs.title: Config conflicts
docs.text:
If both the card and the unit changed the same config, mibpkg refuses to guess. Open the package page and choose:

  • keep the current — the unit's file wins;
  • use the card's — the card's file wins.

From the command line:

mibpkg config-resolve <name> keep
mibpkg config-resolve <name> card
mibpkg config-resolve <name> keep <path>

--config=keep|card on install, rescan and update-all settles conflicts for that run.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Each package's stdout/stderr is captured under /tmp/mibpkg.<package>.<service>.log. The web interface shows it under Installed → package → Logs. More → Logs has the web server and supervisor logs.

/tmp is RAM: logs are capped and disappear on reboot.

From the command line:

mibpkg status
mibpkg list

docs.title: Restart a service
docs.text:
From the package page: Restart.

From the command line:

mibpkg restart <name>

The supervisor restarts the package's services without reinstalling it.

docs.title: Rescan
docs.text:
After changing the SD card, open More → Rescan or run:

mibpkg rescan

Rescan reloads collections and imports new card configs. It does not install anything.

docs.title: GitHub Action
docs.text: The repository ships a composite action, complex256/mibpkg@v1, that builds packages and publishes a GitHub release cars can update from.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
mibpkg new writes .github/workflows/mibpkg-release.yml:

name: mibpkg release
on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']
permissions:
  contents: write
jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # Build your program into the package directory first.
      - uses: complex256/mibpkg@v1
        with:
          packages: .

Push a tag:

git tag v1.0.0
git push --tags

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Meaning packages . Space-separated package directories or .mpk files tag the pushed tag Release tag args empty Extra mibpkg release flags (--id, --name, --keep, ...)

docs.title: First release
docs.text:
The first release needs a collection id and name:

- uses: complex256/mibpkg@v1
  with:
    packages: .
    args: --id my-packages --name "My packages"

Later releases reuse the published collection.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Downloads the Linux host mibpkg from the mibpkg release.
  2. Runs mibpkg release <packages> --repo <this repo> --tag <tag> ... --publish.
  3. Creates the GitHub release with index.json and the package files.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The workflow needs contents: write to create the release.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Publishing a collection
  • Your first package

docs.title: Online sources
docs.text: mibpkg can read package collections from a GitHub release. A car with internet checks them for updates.

docs.title: Add a source
docs.text:
More → Sources → Add source, then enter:

github:owner/repo

The repository must publish a release with an index.json and .mpk assets. The mibpkg release command and the GitHub Action produce that layout.

The official collection is github:complex256/mibpkg-packages. It is built in and always enabled.

docs.title: What the car fetches
docs.text:
For github:owner/repo, mibpkg downloads:

https://github.com/owner/repo/releases/latest/download/index.json

The index lists each package's name, version, file, SHA-256, size, compatibility and plugin metadata. The package files are downloaded from the same release (or from absolute https:// URLs in the index).

docs.title: The card's source list
docs.text:
A card can carry mibpkg/sources.toml:

[[source]]
name = "My packages"
source = "github:owner/repo"

Sources on the card appear under Available without a rescan. More → Sources can enable, disable or remove them.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: The supervisor checks online sources when the car has internet. Updates → Update all installs newer compatible versions. A plugin that adds a permission must be updated individually so the approval sheet can be shown.

docs.title: Verify a collection
docs.text:
Before pointing cars at a repository, check what they will see:

mibpkg verify github:owner/repo
mibpkg verify github:owner/repo --latest
mibpkg verify github:owner/repo --unit MHI2Q

verify reports missing packages, bad checksums, version problems and incompatible entries. It exits non-zero when there are problems.

docs.title: TLS and time
docs.text: Online updates use the unit's TLS stack through libcurl and the CA bundle installed with mibpkg. The unit's clock is unset at boot, so mibpkg uses SNTP to establish a verification time. A car that has never had a working network may need an online check after the clock is set.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check No updates Is the source enabled? Does the release have index.json? Checksum mismatch Re-run mibpkg release; do not edit a published asset TLS error Is the clock set? Is ca.pem present? 404 The repository or release tag is wrong, or the release is still propagating

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: A package is a .mpk: a gzip'd tar with a manifest.toml and its payload. mibpkg keeps every installed version until it needs the space, so a rollback is usually one tap.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
From the web interface: Discover → package → Install.

From the command line:

mibpkg install <name> [collection]
mibpkg install-file <name> <upload-id> [collection|-]

install-file is what the web upload and the phone flow use: the file is in /tmp/mibpkg.upload.<id>.mpk and is consumed once.

A plugin package asks for its permissions. Without an approval list, mibpkg prints the permissions and exits 3:

mibpkg install tailscale --approve=network,ui.slot.statusbar

update-all never approves on your behalf.

docs.title: Where a package comes from
docs.text:
mibpkg loads collections from:

  • the card: mibpkg/collections/<id>/;
  • the seed collection installed with mibpkg;
  • online sources (github:owner/repo).

The same package name can exist in several collections. mibpkg prefers the collection it came from on updates; a fresh install asks when several match.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
mibpkg update-all
mibpkg install <name>

An update keeps the package's config unless both the card and the unit changed it; see Config, logs and restart. A version is never reused: publish a higher version for every change.

docs.title: Roll back
docs.text:
mibpkg rollback <name>

The previous version is kept after an update. Rolling back restores its files, services, config handling and — for a plugin — its jar, grants and icons. Grants never grow on a rollback; a permission that only the previous version declares needs approval.

docs.title: Remove
docs.text:
mibpkg remove <name>
mibpkg remove <name> --purge

Removal stops the services and deletes the package files. --purge also deletes the package's config and data. For a plugin, data is kept unless purged; the jar, grants line, icon directory and status-line settings are removed.

docs.title: Services and config
docs.text:
A package may declare:

  • [[file]] — files copied into the package directory;
  • [[config]] — writable config files under mibpkg/config/<name>/;
  • [[service]] — programs the supervisor starts and restarts;
  • [scripts] — post_install and pre_remove hooks.

See manifest.toml and Service conditions.

docs.title: One package per product
docs.text:
A product's native daemon and its SDK status plugin can ship together in one package:

[package]
name = "tailscale"

[[file]]
src = "bin/tailscaled"
mode = "755"

[[service]]
name = "tailscale"
exec = "@pkg/bin/tailscale.sh"

[plugin]
id = "tailscale-status"
jar = "tailscale-status.jar"
api = 6
permissions = ["network", "ui.slot.statusbar"]

Installing tailscale installs the service and the status plugin in one transaction. Removing it removes both. See Real packages.

docs.title: Plugin packages
docs.text:
A plugin package is a .mpk that carries one SDK plugin. It is declarative: the manifest names the jar, the plugin API level, its permissions and its icons. The SDK runtime loads the jar; mibpkg installs it.

Plugin-only packages are built with the mibsdk plugin build: the mibsdk.plugin Gradle convention produces the stamped jar and the .mpk.

docs.title: Manifest
docs.text:
[package]
name = "carmqtt-status"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "MQTT status item and page"

[compat]
units = ["MHI2Q"]

[plugin]
jar = "carmqtt-status.jar"
api = 6
permissions = ["network", "ui.slot.statusbar"]
icons = ["mqtt-on", "mqtt-off"]
Field Meaning jar The jar at the package root; its stamp is <jar>.stamp api The newest plugin API the plugin uses permissions The permissions the user approves icons PNGs at icons/<name>.png, at most 8

A product package can add id when the plugin id differs from the package name. See Real packages.

docs.title: Build one
docs.text:
From an SDK plugin project:

./gradlew mibpkgPackage -Pmibsdk.mibpkg=/path/to/mibpkg

Output: build/mibsdk/<id>-<version>.mpk.

The jar, its stamp and the icons are also available separately for a combined product package.

docs.title: Install it
docs.text:
1. Install the SDK package (mibsdk) first. A plugin needs the runtime.
  2. Install the plugin .mpk from Discover, More → Install from file, or mibpkg install-file.
  3. Review the permissions and approve.

mibpkg checks:

  • the SDK is installed and supports the plugin's api;
  • the unit's HMI build is one the SDK lists;
  • every declared permission is in the installed SDK catalog;
  • every icon exists and passes the PNG rules;
  • the jar's stamp is valid.

A plugin that asks for a permission the user has not approved is installed but stays BLOCKED_PERMISSIONS until it is granted. The approval sheet normally prevents that: the install stops with exit 3 until the permissions are approved.

docs.title: Update and remove
docs.text:
Update by installing a higher version. The SDK runtime hot-loads the new jar.

mibpkg remove <plugin-or-product>

For a plugin-only package, removal deletes the jar, its grants line, its icons and its status-line settings. Its data is kept unless --purge is used. For a combined product package, removal takes the native service too.

docs.title: Permissions and revocation
docs.text:
A plugin runs only when all of its declared permissions are granted. Revoking one stops the plugin until it is granted again. Grant from the plugin's page in the web interface, or:

mibpkg sdk grant <plugin-id> network,ui.slot.statusbar
mibpkg sdk grant <plugin-id> ""

docs.title: Publishing a collection
docs.text: A collection is a GitHub release with an index.json and the .mpk files. Cars add it as github:owner/repo and check for updates when they have internet.

docs.title: First release
docs.text:
mibpkg release . \
  --repo <owner>/<repo> \
  --tag v0.1.0 \
  --id my-packages \
  --name "My packages" \
  --publish
Flag Meaning --repo owner/repo that will host the release --tag Release tag; use v + semver --id Collection id, [a-z0-9-]{1,40} --name Human name shown in the web interface --keep How many versions of each package to keep (default 3) --out Output directory (default out/release-<tag>) --asset Extra file to attach (for example sources.json) --publish Create the GitHub release and wait for the index to be live

The first release must pass --id. Later releases reuse the published id unless you pass --new-id.

docs.title: What it writes
docs.text:
out/release-v0.1.0/
├── index.json
├── hello-0.1.0.mpk
└── ...

index.json lists every package version kept, with an absolute download URL, SHA-256 and size. Older versions are carried forward, so a car can still roll back to them.

docs.title: Later releases
docs.text:
mibpkg release . --repo <owner>/<repo> --tag v0.2.0 --publish

The collection id and name are read from the previous release. --keep defaults to 3 versions per package. A version already published with different contents is refused: bump the version.

docs.title: GitHub CLI
docs.text: mibpkg release uses gh. Install the GitHub CLI and run gh auth login, or set GH_TOKEN.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
mibpkg verify out/release-v0.2.0
mibpkg verify github:<owner>/<repo> --latest

verify checks the index, file names, checksums, versions, compatibility and plugin metadata. It exits non-zero on problems.

docs.title: Publish the source list
docs.text: The optional sources.json asset tells new cars which collections to offer. mibpkg new and the official collection include one. Attach it with --asset packaging/sources.json.

docs.title: Real packages
docs.text:
These packages in the mib2q-plugins repository show the two package shapes mibpkg supports.

Product Package Shape What it shows mib2q-tailscale tailscale native + [plugin] Multiple binaries, optional configs, a service that waits for internet, and an icon-only status item mib2q-carmqtt carmqtt native + [plugin] A required config, a service that waits for the tailnet, and a status item/page mib2q-wireguard wireguard native A config example and a service with an internet start condition bike-rack bike-rack [plugin] Vehicle permissions and a parking override hello-menu hello-menu [plugin] A Car row, a page and a status item inputs-demo inputs-demo [plugin] Every native input

docs.title: One package, two halves
docs.text: The Tailscale and carmqtt products ship the native daemon and the SDK status plugin in one .mpk. The package name is the product; the plugin's own id is in [plugin].id.

docs.title: Tailscale
docs.text:
[package]
name = "tailscale"
version = "1.102.5"

[[file]]
src = "bin/tailscaled"
mode = "755"

[[service]]
name = "tailscale"
exec = "@pkg/bin/tailscale.sh"
args = ["serve", "@config"]
restart = "always"
after = ["internet"]
after_timeout = "5m"

[plugin]
id = "tailscale-status"
jar = "tailscale-status.jar"
api = 6
permissions = ["network", "ui.slot.statusbar"]
icons = ["tailscale-on", "tailscale-off"]

The package's files install under its own package directory; the plugin half installs as plugins/tailscale-status.jar. The service and the status item are one version and one removal.

docs.title: carmqtt
docs.text:
[package]
name = "carmqtt"
version = "0.2.2"

[[file]]
src = "bin/carmqtt"
mode = "755"

[[config]]
path = "carmqtt.toml"
example = "carmqtt.toml.example"
required = true

[[service]]
name = "carmqtt"
exec = "@pkg/bin/carmqtt"
args = ["--config", "@config/carmqtt.toml"]
restart = "always"
after = ["tailnet"]
after_timeout = "5m"

[plugin]
id = "carmqtt-status"
jar = "carmqtt-status.jar"
api = 6
permissions = ["network", "ui.slot.statusbar"]
icons = ["mqtt-on", "mqtt-off"]

A required config means the service will not start until mibpkg/config/carmqtt/carmqtt.toml exists. The package page shows the missing config and offers an editor.

docs.title: Native only
docs.text:
wireguard has no SDK plugin. It is a normal package with one service and a required config:

[[service]]
name = "mibwg"
exec = "@pkg/bin/mibwg.sh"
args = ["serve", "@config/mibwg.conf"]
restart = "always"
after = ["internet"]
after_timeout = "5m"

docs.title: Plugin only
docs.text:
The SDK samples are ordinary [plugin] packages. hello-menu shows the smallest useful page:

[package]
name = "hello-menu"
version = "1.102.5"

[plugin]
jar = "hello-menu.jar"
api = 6
permissions = ["ui.slot.carmenu", "ui.slot.statusbar"]
icons = ["hello", "hello-20"]

See the SDK docs for writing the plugin and Plugin packages for installing one.

docs.title: Building a product package
docs.text:
A product package is a staging directory with the native payload and the plugin stage:

tailscale-1.102.5.mpk
├── manifest.toml
├── bin/
│   ├── tailscaled
│   ├── tailscale
│   ├── sntp
│   ├── tsstatus
│   └── libtsclock.so
├── authkey.example
├── accept-routes.example
├── tailscale-status.jar
├── tailscale-status.jar.stamp
└── icons/
    ├── tailscale-on.png
    └── tailscale-off.png

mibpkg build tailscale-stage out
mibpkg index out --id my-products --name "My products" --flat
mibpkg verify out

The repository's Gradle packageDaemon tasks assemble this from the daemon and plugin builds.

docs.title: Stop everything with DISABLE
docs.text:
Create an empty file:

<mibpkg SD card>/mibpkg/DISABLE

Reboot. The boot hook logs it and starts no package services, no supervisor and no web server. The stock system is unaffected. Remove the file and reboot to resume.

This is the first thing to try if a package is misbehaving.

docs.title: GEM recovery buttons
docs.text:
Open GEM → mibpkg:

Button What it does Remove PIN Clears the web PIN and restarts the web server Reset web settings Deletes web.toml, restores defaults and restarts the web server Remove mibpkg Uninstalls mibpkg, restoring stock files

docs.title: Package-level recovery
docs.text:
Open Installed → package:

  • Restart — restart its services;
  • Rollback — switch to the previous version;
  • Logs — see why it failed;
  • Remove — remove it; data is kept unless you choose to purge.

docs.title: mibpkg will not start
docs.text:
1. Check the card has mibpkg/ and that DISABLE is not present.
  2. Check More → Health or mibpkg status if the web interface works.
  3. Reinstall mibpkg from the card. The installer is idempotent.
  4. If the unit is unresponsive, remove the card and reboot; the stock boot path does not need mibpkg.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
GEM → mibpkg → Remove mibpkg, or:

mibpkg uninstall-self

Uninstall restores the stock files mibpkg backed up. It refuses while packages, plugins or vehicle overrides are active; remove those first.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The SD-card option is greyed out.

The card is not FAT32 on a Master Boot Record partition. Reformat it; GUID/GPT is not readable by the update menu.

"MOST considered unstable" popup.

On a bench or a car without a live MOST bus, the unit can flag the bus unstable. mibpkg suppresses it; a single popup right after install may still appear and should not return.

The unit keeps returning to the software-update summary.

Pull the SD card and restart the car. It will boot normally.

The GEM tile is missing.

The engineering menu reads its setting at boot. On a fresh install it can take one more normal reboot for the tile to appear. The web interface is available in the meantime if the unit is reachable.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: Symptom Check Package not listed Is it in a loaded collection? More → Sources and Rescan not compatible with this unit The package's [compat] does not match the unit checksum mismatch The .mpk changed after the index was written; republish it needs permission approval Install with Install (web) or --approve=...; exit 3 Plugin BLOCKED_PERMISSIONS Grant every declared permission on the plugin page Service does not start Check the package logs and its after conditions needs config Put the file in mibpkg/config/<name>/ on the card, then Rescan Update fails The previous version is still active; read the job output

docs.title: Web interface
docs.text: Symptom Check Page unreachable Join the hotspot or Tailscale; check Web settings 409 busy Another action (web or GEM) is running; wait Upload expired Uploads last 10 minutes; upload again Wrong PIN GEM → mibpkg → Remove PIN Locked out after a settings change GEM → mibpkg → Reset web settings Port changed, no page Reboot once so the firewall rule is active

docs.title: mibpkg itself
docs.text:
mibpkg status
mibpkg list

More → Health shows the installed version, the supervisor's version, disk space and service state.

If the web server will not come back, GEM → mibpkg → Reset web settings, or reinstall mibpkg from the card.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
Open an issue with:

  • the unit model (MHI2/MHI2Q) and version line;
  • the mibpkg version;
  • the package name and version;
  • the job output or package log;
  • whether the web interface and GEM are reachable.

Remove any personal data before posting logs.

docs.title: Web interface
docs.text: The web interface is the main way to use mibpkg. It is served by the car, so it works from a phone on the hotspot or from a laptop on the tailnet.

docs.title: Open it
docs.text:
1. Join the car's Wi-Fi hotspot, or reach the car over Tailscale.
  2. In the car, open GEM → mibpkg for the address (for example http://10.255.1.1).
  3. Open the address in a browser.

By default mibpkg listens only on the hotspot and Tailscale. More → Web settings changes that.

docs.title: The four tabs
docs.text: Tab What it is for Discover Packages on the card and in online collections Updates Packages with a newer version, and Update all Installed What is installed: inspect, configure, restart, roll back, remove More Install from file, logs, sources, web settings, health

docs.title: Discover
docs.text: Browse by collection. A package page shows its version, description, compatibility, size, services, configs and — for a plugin — the permissions it asks for. Install starts a job.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: A row appears when a newer compatible version is in a loaded collection. Update all updates every package that needs no new permission approval. A plugin update that adds a permission must be updated individually so the approval sheet can be shown.

docs.title: Installed
docs.text:
The package page has:

  • Open — the package's own page or service status, when it has one.
  • Configs — edit a config file.
  • Logs — follow the package's log.
  • Restart — restart its services.
  • Rollback — switch to the previous version, if one is kept.
  • Remove — remove the package; remove and delete data purges its data.

docs.title: More
docs.text:
• Install from file — upload a .mpk from the phone.
  • Logs — the web server, supervisor and package logs.
  • Sources — online collections and the card's sources.toml.
  • Web settings — listen addresses, port, hotspot interface and PIN.
  • Health — versions, disk, supervisor and service state.

docs.title: Jobs and busy states
docs.text:
An action runs as a job. The page follows it and shows its output. Only one action runs at a time:

  • a second web action gets 409 busy and the id of the running job;
  • an action while GEM is running gets busy too.

Wait for the running job to finish, then retry. A reloaded page reattaches to the running job.

docs.title: Uploads
docs.text:
More → Install from file streams the file to the car and inspects it before installing. It shows:

  • the package name and version;
  • whether it is new, an upgrade, the same version, or older;
  • compatibility with this unit;
  • services and scripts;
  • permissions the plugin asks for, and which ones need approval.

Uploads expire after 10 minutes. Install or discard them.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: A plugin's permissions are shown one per row in plain words. Install only continues when the sheet is approved. A permission the user revoked stays revoked, even if the package is installed again, until it is granted on the plugin's page.

docs.title: Web settings and PIN
docs.text: Open More → Web settings.

docs.title: Listen addresses
docs.text:
By default the web interface answers on:

  • hotspot — the car's Wi-Fi access point;
  • tailnet — Tailscale.

It does not answer on the SIM data link. You can enable or disable each class.

docs.title: Port
docs.text: The default is 80. If you change it, the page shows the new URL after the web server restarts. Port 8080 is used by a stock process and is not a good choice.

docs.title: Hotspot interface
docs.text: mibpkg recognises the hotspot interface by name (uap*). If your unit names it differently, choose the interface in Web settings. A wrong interface can make the web page unreachable from the hotspot.

docs.title: PIN
docs.text:
A PIN is 4 to 12 digits. Set it under Web settings. It is required after every web-server restart, including a self-update.

Forgot the PIN? GEM → mibpkg → Remove PIN.

Locked out by a wrong listen/port setting? GEM → mibpkg → Reset web settings. This deletes web.toml, restores defaults and restarts the web server.

docs.title: Firewall
docs.text:
The web server asks mibpkg to add a pass rule for its port on the hotspot interface. The rule is written to pf.conf on flash and takes effect on the next boot. mibpkg never reloads pf.conf at runtime: doing so resets the stock anchors and can cut off the hotspot's internet.

If the page is unreachable after changing the port, reboot once so the firewall rule is active.

docs.title: Confirmation
docs.text: Saving settings that would make the current connection unable to reach the page returns a needs_confirm warning. Confirm the save only if you have another way in (the car's screen or Tailscale).

docs.title: Your first package
docs.text: This tutorial builds a small package with one service, packs it, installs it, and publishes a collection cars can update from.

docs.title: 1. Scaffold
docs.text:
mibpkg new hello
cd hello

The generated tree:

hello/
├── manifest.toml
├── bin/hello                  executable sample service
├── README.md
├── .gitignore
└── .github/workflows/mibpkg-release.yml

manifest.toml is already valid:

[package]
name = "hello"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "What hello does, in one line"

[[file]]
src = "bin/hello"
mode = "755"

[[service]]
name = "hello"
exec = "@pkg/bin/hello"

bin/hello is a shell loop. Replace it with your program, or point exec at another file in bin/.

docs.title: 2. Build
docs.text:
mibpkg build . out

Output:

out/hello-0.1.0.mpk

The .mpk is a gzip'd tar with manifest.toml and the payload. Inspect it with:

tar tzf out/hello-0.1.0.mpk

docs.title: 3. Install it on the unit
docs.text:
Copy the .mpk to the card, or upload it from a phone:

  1. Open the web interface.
  2. More → Install from file.
  3. Choose hello-0.1.0.mpk.
  4. Review the package and install.

The package page shows the service state and its logs. The service starts after install and is supervised at boot.

docs.title: 4. Add a config
docs.text:
[[file]]
src = "hello.conf.example"

[[config]]
path = "hello.conf"
example = "hello.conf.example"
required = true

A required config makes the package page show needs config until you create mibpkg/config/hello/hello.conf on the card and rescan.

docs.title: 5. Add a start condition
docs.text:
[[service]]
name = "hello"
exec = "@pkg/bin/hello"
after = ["internet"]
after_timeout = "5m"

The supervisor waits for the condition, or starts anyway after 5 minutes. Aliases and raw checks are in Service conditions.

docs.title: 6. Package a native program with an SDK plugin
docs.text:
A product can carry both a native service and an SDK status plugin in one .mpk:

[plugin]
id = "hello-status"
jar = "hello-status.jar"
api = 6
permissions = ["ui.slot.statusbar"]
icons = ["hello-20"]

The package needs hello-status.jar, its .stamp and icons/hello-20.png at the root. See Real packages.

docs.title: 7. Publish
docs.text:
Create a repository and run:

mibpkg release . \
  --repo <owner>/hello \
  --tag v0.1.0 \
  --id my-packages \
  --name "My packages" \
  --publish

This builds the package, writes index.json, creates the GitHub release, uploads the files and waits for the index to become live. See Publishing a collection.

Cars add:

github:<owner>/hello

in More → Sources.

docs.title: 8. Check what cars see
docs.text: mibpkg verify github:<owner>/hello

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
mibpkg has host commands (build and publish) and on-unit commands (install, supervise, web).

mibpkg [--root DIR] [--no-supervisor] <command>
Global flag Meaning --root DIR Operate on a fake root; used by tests and development --no-supervisor Do not start or reload the supervisor after an action

docs.title: Host commands
docs.text: Command What it does mibpkg build <src-dir> <out-dir> Build <name>-<version>.mpk from a directory with manifest.toml mibpkg index <collection-dir> --id ID --name NAME [--flat] Write index.json for a collection mibpkg release <input>... --repo OWNER/REPO --tag TAG [opts] Build a release and optionally publish it mibpkg verify <source> [--latest] [--unit MHI2Q] Check a collection or SWDL card the way a car would mibpkg new <name> [--dir DIR] Scaffold a buildable package mibpkg swdl-card <out> --payload DIR [--seed DIR] --version V [opts] Assemble an SD-card installer mibpkg gem-patch build --stock JAR --patched JAR [--out DIR] Build a GEM patch set

docs.title: build
docs.text:
mibpkg build . out

Validates manifest.toml, checks every declared file exists, then writes out/<name>-<version>.mpk. It refuses symlinks, unsafe paths and packages over 128 MiB unpacked.

docs.title: index
docs.text:
mibpkg index my-collection --id my-packages --name "My packages"
mibpkg index flat-dir --id my-packages --name "My packages" --flat

Reads packages/*.mpk (or the directory itself with --flat), checks names and versions, and writes index.json.

docs.title: release
docs.text:
mibpkg release pkg/ other.mpk \
  --repo owner/repo \
  --tag v1.2.0 \
  --id my-packages \
  --name "My packages" \
  --keep 3 \
  --publish
Option Meaning --repo owner/repo (required) --tag Release tag (required) --id Collection id; required on the first release --name Human name --new-id Allow changing the collection id --keep Versions per package to keep (default 3) --out Output directory (default out/release-<tag>) --asset Extra file to attach --publish Create the GitHub release

docs.title: verify
docs.text:
mibpkg verify github:owner/repo
mibpkg verify github:owner/repo --latest
mibpkg verify out/release-v1.2.0
mibpkg verify /path/to/card
mibpkg verify --unit MHI2Q github:owner/repo

Exits non-zero when a package is missing, a checksum is wrong, a version is invalid or a package is incompatible with --unit.

docs.title: new
docs.text:
mibpkg new hello
mibpkg new hello --dir projects/hello

Writes a manifest, a runnable sample service, a README, .gitignore and a release workflow. See Your first package.

docs.title: swdl-card
docs.text:
mibpkg swdl-card out/card \
  --payload payload/ \
  --seed seed/ \
  --version 1.0.0 \
  --signed-header header.txt

--no-mib omits the custom-script path. Without a signed header the card works through the custom-script method, but the engineering-menu entry will not be accepted.

docs.title: Package actions
docs.text:
mibpkg list
mibpkg status
mibpkg install <name> [collection]
mibpkg install-file <name> <upload-id> [collection|-]
mibpkg remove <name> [--purge|--purge-data] [--force]
mibpkg rollback <name> [--approve=<perm,...>]
mibpkg restart <name>
mibpkg rescan
mibpkg update-all
mibpkg config-resolve <name> keep|card [path]
Flag Meaning --approve=<perm,...> Approve a plugin's permissions --purge, --purge-data Delete config and data on removal --force Override a refusal (for example a pending override) --config=keep\|card Settle config conflicts on install, rescan, update-all

An install or update that needs permission approval exits 3 and lists the permissions.

docs.title: SD card and online
docs.text:
mibpkg rescan
mibpkg online-check
mibpkg sntp [host:port]

docs.title: Web server
docs.text:
mibpkg web

Runs the web server in the foreground. The supervisor normally runs it as mibpkg.web.

docs.title: SDK verbs
docs.text:
mibpkg sdk status
mibpkg sdk grant <plugin-id> <perm,...>
mibpkg sdk push <plugin-id>
mibpkg sdk remove <plugin-id> [--purge]
mibpkg sdk safe-mode on|off
mibpkg sdk boot-state set-wrap <n>
mibpkg sdk data-clear <plugin-id>

A bundled plugin cannot be removed with sdk remove; remove its product package instead.

docs.title: Installer and GEM
docs.text:
mibpkg bootstrap
mibpkg enable-gem
mibpkg disable-gem
mibpkg gem-patch apply|status|revert [--from DIR]
mibpkg uninstall-self [--purge] [--force]
mibpkg supervise

supervise is the long-running supervisor; the boot hook starts it.

docs.title: GEM actions
docs.text:
The GEM buttons call:

mibpkg gem install|install-file|remove|rollback|restart|self-update|config-set|config-resolve|sdk
mibpkg gem source-add|source-remove|web-settings|web-reset|web-restart|web-clear-pin

These record OK: or FAILED: in the GEM screen. A busy lock shows BUSY: and changes nothing.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Failed, or verify found problems 2 Bad usage 3 Permissions need approval

A GEM action exits 0 even when its result is FAILED:; the screen carries the result. The web API uses HTTP status codes and job results.

docs.title: Collection index
docs.text: A collection is a directory with index.json and package files. Online collections are GitHub releases with the same layout.

docs.title: Directory
docs.text:
my-collection/
├── index.json
└── packages/
    ├── hello-1.0.0.mpk
    └── hello-1.1.0.mpk

A flat collection puts the .mpk files next to index.json and uses --flat with mibpkg index.

docs.title: index.json
docs.text:
{
  "format": 1,
  "collection": {
    "id": "my-packages",
    "name": "My packages"
  },
  "packages": [
    {
      "name": "hello",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "file": "packages/hello-1.0.0.mpk",
      "sha256": "…",
      "size": 12345,
      "description": "Hello package",
      "compat": { "units": ["MHI2Q"] },
      "uses_scripts": false
    }
  ],
  "signatures": []
}
Field Meaning format 1 collection.id [a-z0-9-]{1,40}; uploaded is reserved collection.name Shown in the web interface packages[].name Package name packages[].version Semver packages[].file Relative path or absolute https:// URL packages[].sha256 Lowercase hex SHA-256 packages[].size Bytes packages[].compat Same shape as [compat] packages[].uses_scripts Whether the package runs scripts packages[].kind plugin or sdk, absent for a plain package packages[].permissions A plugin's declared permissions signatures Reserved; ignored in v1

docs.title: Build it
docs.text:
mibpkg index my-collection --id my-packages --name "My packages"

The collection id and name are validated. Each file name must be <name>-<version>.mpk and match the manifest inside.

docs.title: Online URLs
docs.text: An online index may use absolute https:// URLs in file. A relative path resolves against the release's download directory. mibpkg release writes absolute URLs for every release asset.

docs.title: Source list
docs.text:
A card can carry mibpkg/sources.toml:

[[source]]
name = "My packages"
source = "github:owner/repo"

mibpkg release can attach a sources.json asset with the same entries; new cars read it from the official collection.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
mibpkg verify my-collection
mibpkg verify github:owner/repo --latest

verify checks the index format, file names, checksums, versions, compatibility and plugin metadata.

docs.title: manifest.toml
docs.text:
Every .mpk contains a manifest.toml. It describes the package, its files, services, configs and — for SDK packages — the plugin or SDK metadata.

[package]
name = "hello"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "One line shown in the web interface"

[compat]
units = ["MHI2Q"]

[[file]]
src = "bin/hello"
mode = "755"

[[service]]
name = "hello"
exec = "@pkg/bin/hello"
restart = "always"

docs.title: [package]
docs.text:
Field Required Rules name Yes 1–40 characters, [a-z0-9-], starting with a letter or digit. Reserved: restart, reload, stop, selfupdate, pid, lock, status, log, rw, rwlock, uploaded version Yes Semver (1.2.3, 1.2.3-beta.1). A version is never reused description No One line

mibsdk is reserved for the SDK package. Only a manifest with [sdk] may use it.

docs.title: [compat]
docs.text:
Field Meaning units Unit models that may install the package, e.g. ["MHI2Q"] firmware Firmware strings the package accepts

Omit a list to allow everything.

docs.title: [[file]]
docs.text:
Field Meaning src A relative path inside the package mode Octal mode, default 644; use 755 for programs

Every src must exist in the package. Symlinks and .. are refused.

Files are installed under the package directory:

/mnt/app/root/mibpkg/pkgs/<name>/<version>/<src>

docs.title: [[config]]
docs.text:
Field Meaning path Path below the package's config directory example Optional example file shipped in the package required The service will not start until the file exists

The live file lives at:

/mnt/app/root/mibpkg/state/config/<name>/<path>

A card can supply it at mibpkg/config/<name>/<path>. If both the card and the unit changed it, config-resolve or --config=keep|card settles the conflict.

docs.title: [[service]]
docs.text:
Field Meaning name 1–40 [a-z0-9-], unique within the package exec Must start with @pkg/ and name a file in [[file]] args Arguments; @pkg and @config are expanded phase Currently only default restart always (default), on-failure, never after Start conditions; all must hold after_timeout Start anyway after 30s, 5m, 2h (1 s–24 h)

See Service conditions.

docs.title: [scripts]
docs.text:
Field Meaning post_install Runs after the files are staged, before the version is committed pre_remove Runs before removal; a failure leaves the package installed

Scripts are relative paths inside the package. They run with a timeout.

docs.title: [plugin]
docs.text:
A plugin package carries one SDK plugin. It may be plugin-only, or combined with native files, configs, services and scripts.

Field Required Meaning id No Plugin id; defaults to the package name. 2–40 [a-z0-9-] jar Yes Must be <id>.jar api Yes Newest plugin API level; at least 1 permissions Yes Permission ids icons No Icon names, [a-z0-9-]{1,32}, at most 8; each needs icons/<name>.png 
[package]
name = "carmqtt"
version = "1.2.0"

[[file]]
src = "bin/carmqtt"
mode = "755"

[[service]]
name = "carmqtt"
exec = "@pkg/bin/carmqtt"
args = ["--config", "@config/carmqtt.toml"]
after = ["tailnet"]

[plugin]
id = "carmqtt-status"
jar = "carmqtt-status.jar"
api = 6
permissions = ["network", "ui.slot.statusbar"]
icons = ["mqtt-on", "mqtt-off"]

The plugin jar and its .stamp are installed as plugins/<id>.jar; the icons as icons/<id>/<sha16>.png. The package name remains the install/update identity.

docs.title: [sdk]
docs.text:
Reserved for the SDK package (name = "mibsdk"). It is declarative: no files, services, configs or scripts.

Field Meaning api, min_api Plugin API range hmi HMI builds the SDK supports jars SDK jars, names starting mibsdk- stamp One stamp for all jars configurator Configurator class bundle Bundle-list line, <name>=<class> tracer_configurator DSITracer configurator class hmicar_stock, hmicar HMICar= line, before/after hmisystem_stock, hmisystem Optional HMISystem= line, both or neither owned Class paths only the SDK may define properties sdk.properties lines permissions Permission catalog file icons Built-in icon names, at most 32

docs.title: [[patch]]
docs.text: Reserved; not implemented. A package using it is refused with “requires a newer mibpkg”.

docs.title: Placeholders
docs.text: Placeholder Expands to @pkg The installed package version directory @config The package's config directory

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text: A package has two layouts: the source directory you build, and the directory mibpkg installs.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
hello/
├── manifest.toml
├── bin/
│   └── hello
├── hello.conf.example
├── icons/
│   ├── hello.png
│   └── hello-20.png
├── hello-status.jar
├── hello-status.jar.stamp
├── README.md
└── .github/workflows/mibpkg-release.yml
Path Purpose manifest.toml Package metadata and payload list bin/ Programs copied to the package directory *.example Config examples icons/ Plugin icons, declared in [plugin].icons <id>.jar + <id>.jar.stamp Plugin payload README.md Repository documentation, not installed

mibpkg build includes every regular file in the directory except dotfiles. It refuses symlinks.

docs.title: The .mpk
docs.text:
hello-1.0.0.mpk                 gzip'd ustar
├── manifest.toml
├── bin/hello
├── hello.conf.example
├── hello-status.jar
├── hello-status.jar.stamp
└── icons/hello.png

Limits: 128 MiB unpacked, individual paths up to 100 bytes, files only (no symlinks/devices).

docs.title: On the unit
docs.text: Path Contents /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/ mibpkg home /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/pkgs/<name>/<version>/ The installed package files /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/pkgs/<name>/current The active version /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/state/config/<name>/ Live config files /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/state/backups/ Once-only stock-file backups /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/state/ State, boot entries, GEM data /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/boot.d/ Boot scripts /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/gem/ Generated GEM screens /mnt/persist/mibsdk/ SDK plugin data /tmp/mibpkg.<name>.<service>.log Service stdout/stderr /tmp/mibpkg.log Action log (RAM)

docs.title: Product package with an SDK plugin
docs.text:
pkgs/tailscale/1.102.5/
├── manifest.toml
├── bin/tailscaled
├── bin/tailscale
└── ...

/mnt/app/eso/hmi/lsd/mibsdk/
├── plugins/tailscale-status.jar
├── icons/tailscale-status/<sha16>.png
└── grants.properties

The native half is under pkgs/tailscale; the plugin half is in the SDK's directories under its own plugin id. Both belong to the tailscale package: one version, one removal.

docs.title: Versions and rollback
docs.text:
mibpkg keeps the current version and the previous version:

pkgs/tailscale/
├── current              contains "1.102.5"
├── 1.3.0/
└── 1.102.5/

Rollback switches current and restores that version's files, services and plugin half.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
Path What lives there /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/ mibpkg home: packages, state, boot scripts, GEM screens /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/pkgs/<name>/<version>/ Installed package files /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/pkgs/<name>/current Active version /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/state/config/<name>/ Live config files /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/state/backups/ Once-only backups of stock files /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/boot.d/ Boot entries /mnt/app/root/mibpkg/gem/ Generated GEM screens /mnt/persist/mibsdk/ SDK plugin data /mnt/app/eso/hmi/lsd/mibsdk/ SDK install root /mnt/app/eso/hmi/lsd/jars/ SDK jars /tmp/mibpkg.log Action log (RAM) /tmp/mibpkg.<name>.<service>.log Service stdout/stderr /tmp/mibpkg.<name>.* Runtime markers, uploads, temp files

/tmp is /dev/shmem: files only, no directories, and everything is lost on reboot.

docs.title: mibpkg status
docs.text: Prints the unit and mibpkg state. It is read-only.

docs.title: mibpkg list
docs.text: Lists installed packages with their version and collection.

docs.title: Web health
docs.text:
More → Health shows:

  • the installed mibpkg version;
  • the supervisor's version;
  • free space;
  • running services;
  • online-source state.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
• More → Logs — web server and supervisor;
  • Installed → package → Logs — one package;
  • /tmp/mibpkg.log — actions;
  • /tmp/mibpkg.<name>.<service>.log — services.

Logs are capped and volatile.

docs.title: Service conditions
docs.text:
A service can wait for a condition before it starts.

[[service]]
name = "carmqtt"
exec = "@pkg/bin/carmqtt"
args = ["--config", "@config/carmqtt.toml"]
restart = "always"
after = ["tailnet"]
after_timeout = "5m"

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text:
Alias Default meaning internet A default route exists tailnet A route to 100.100.100.100 through tun* hmi-ready /tmp/smFlagStartupDone exists

settings.toml [conditions] can override an alias per unit:

[conditions]
hmi-ready = "file:/tmp/startupFinishedFlag"

docs.title: Raw checks
docs.text:
Form Meaning file:/absolute/path The file exists iface:<name> The interface is up and has an address route:<dest>[@<iface prefix>] A route to dest exists, optionally through an interface

Examples:

after = ["file:/mnt/persist/ready", "iface:uap0"]
after = ["route:100.100.100.100@tun"]
after = ["route:192.168.1.0"]

Interface names are 1–15 characters of [a-z0-9].

docs.title: Timeout
docs.text: after_timeout = "30s", "5m" or "2h" starts the service anyway after that time. The range is 1 second to 24 hours. Without it, a service waits indefinitely.

docs.title: Restart policy
docs.text: Value Meaning always Restart whenever it exits (default) on-failure Restart only on a non-zero exit never Do not restart

docs.title: Phases
docs.text: Only the default phase is implemented. A service with another phase is refused with “requires a newer mibpkg”.

docs.title: Supported
docs.text:
Model MIB2 High, MHI2 or MHI2Q OS QNX 6.5 Architecture ARMv7 Shell /bin/ksh as /bin/sh

The unit model is read from the unit, not from the package. mibpkg status and the web health page show it.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
A package can restrict itself:

[compat]
units = ["MHI2Q"]
firmware = ["HMI_AU_MIB2_HQC_NAR_G22_C10_180803"]
  • units matches the model string (MHI2, MHI2Q).
  • firmware matches the HMI build string.
  • Omit a list to allow everything.

mibpkg refuses an incompatible package with a message naming the unit. mibpkg verify --unit MHI2Q checks a collection against a unit before cars see it.

docs.title: Not supported
docs.text:
• Other MIB2 variants.
  • MIB2 Standard, MIB3 and other platforms.
  • Other head-unit families.

The installer and boot hook are specific to the MIB2 High.

docs.title: Web API
docs.text: The web interface is a static page over a JSON API on the car. This page documents the API for contributors and for anyone building another client.

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
Method Path Meaning GET /api/session {pin_required, authed} POST /api/login {pin}; sets a session cookie POST /api/logout Clears the session

A wrong PIN returns 401. Too many wrong PINs returns 429 with retry_after.

docs.title: Status and packages
docs.text: Method Path Meaning GET /api/status Versions, health, current job GET /api/packages Installed and available packages GET /api/packages/<name>/config/<n> Read config n PUT /api/packages/<name>/config/<n> Write config n (UTF-8 text body) GET /api/sources Enabled and available sources POST /api/sources Add {source} DELETE /api/sources Remove {source} GET /api/settings Web settings PUT /api/settings Save web settings GET /api/logs Known logs GET /api/logs/<id>?bytes=N Tail a log POST /api/actions Start an action job GET /api/jobs/<id>?since=N Job state and output

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text: Actions run as jobs. POST /api/actions returns 202 with {job} or 409 with {busy, job, error} when another action is running. Poll the job until ok or error.

docs.title: Uploads
docs.text:
Method Path Meaning POST /api/uploads Stream a .mpk; returns an upload id POST /api/uploads/<id>/install {collection, approve[]} DELETE /api/uploads/<id> Discard

An upload is inspected before install: name, version, kind, compatibility, services, permissions and needs_approval. Uploads expire after 10 minutes.

docs.title: Settings body
docs.text:
{
  "listen": ["hotspot", "tailnet"],
  "port": 80,
  "pin": "1234",
  "clear_pin": false,
  "confirm": false,
  "hotspot_interface": ""
}

If the new settings would make the current connection unable to reach the page, the API returns 409 with needs_confirm. Send confirm: true to save anyway.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Code Meaning 400 Bad request or invalid package 401 Wrong PIN 404 Unknown package, job, upload or config 409 Busy, or settings need confirmation 429 Too many wrong PINs 500 Server-side failure

All errors are JSON with an error field.
